description.value: Cafe MOA — listed on the museum's own website as 'Cedar Café' — is the in-house café at the Museum of Anthropology at UBC, one of Canada's foremost anthropological museums housed in an Arthur Erickson-designed building overlooking the Pacific. The café sits inside the museum, up the ramp from the admission desk, so a cyclist stopping here would be stepping into a world-class cultural institution. The site anchors the end of a scenic but demanding cycling route along NW Marine Drive.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record names this 'Cafe MOA,' but the Museum of Anthropology website consistently calls its in-house café 'Cedar Café' — a clear name mismatch. The website confirms the address (6393 NW Marine Drive, Vancouver) and establishes that the café is inside the museum, located 'up the ramp from the admission desk,' implying museum access is required. The website includes a 'Bike' section in Getting Here with cycling directions but explicitly warns that Mobi bike shares do not serve UBC and that the route involves a significant hill; no bike parking, water refill, washrooms, or other cyclist-specific amenities are confirmed anywhere on the site.
